dedupe_keys.name: swiss post seismic reconnaissance of building damage after the 2023 al haouz morocco earthquake

description: After the magnitude 6.8 earthquake of 8 September 2023 in Morocco, a team of Swiss scientists and engineers visited heavily affected towns and villages 10 to 70 km from the epicentre in the High Atlas Mountains and Marrakech and reported the building damage they inspected. The paper describes the prevalent building typologies, their construction and the resulting structural and non-structural damage patterns, and discusses possible site effects from a review of the seismological and geological setting. Coverage: affected High Atlas villages and Marrakech. Access: open-access article in Scientific Reports (2025), also in PubMed Central. Licence: CC-BY-4.0 article. Caveats: observational reconnaissance of selected sites, not a complete damage census. Outcome: the shallow depth and geological complexity drove the severe impact, the lack of earthquake-resistant construction worsened it, modern structures in Marrakech were largely unaffected, and ancient buildings in the Medina suffered partial damage. Simulation uses: vulnerability curves for earthen and stone masonry, and exposure models for mountain villages in North Africa. Related records: StEER reconnaissance and the Puebla 2017 building damage assessment.

name: Swiss post-seismic reconnaissance of building damage after the 2023 Al Haouz (Morocco) earthquake
organisations: Swiss Seismological Service, ETH Zurich (Afifa Imtiaz)
Earthquake Engineering and Structural Dynamics laboratory (EESD), School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering
Other Swiss institutions in the reconnaissance team
outcomes: Severe damage stemmed from the shallow source and complex geology and was worsened by the lack of earthquake-resistant construction; modern Marrakech buildings were largely unaffected while older Medina buildings were partly damaged, and rural High Atlas masonry suffered most.
resources_used: Field inspection of building damage in towns and villages 10 to 70 km from the epicentre
Literature on the seismological and geological setting
